classification.difficultyReason: Direct substitution into the geometric dot product formula, with one reversed vector requiring a supplementary angle.

content.prompt: Find the dot product to two decimal places.

spec.description: Common-tail vectors: a points up-left and b points right. The upper non-reflex angle is 150 degrees. Source orange angle marks become ordinary black house-style marks.
spec.mathematics: The angle between the directed vectors is 150 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: All diagram content is permanently visible; no answer is drawn.

spec.description: Both vectors point away from their common tail: a up-right and b right. Preserve the source schematic slope and printed 40-degree given. Source orange angle marks become ordinary black house-style marks.
spec.mathematics: The labelled angle between the directed vectors is 40 degrees; the schematic is not a measured-angle construction.
spec.answerVisibility: All diagram content is permanently visible; no answer is drawn.

spec.description: Vector a points down-left into the junction; vector b points right away from it. The printed 40-degree arc lies between the rightward ray and the up-right sloping ray. Source orange angle marks become ordinary black house-style marks.
spec.mathematics: The displayed 40 degrees is supplementary to the 140-degree angle between the directed vectors.
spec.answerVisibility: The reversed arrow and supplied 40-degree angle remain visible. The derived 140-degree angle is solution-only.

answer.worked:
The vector $\underset{\sim}{a}$ points towards the junction, so the angle between the directed vectors is $180^\circ-40^\circ=140^\circ$.

$$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}&=(3)(5)\cos140^\circ\\\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}&\approx-11.49\end{aligned}$$
